blocks.text: 2.4 General Considerations for Administration
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: y PYZCHIVA is intended for use under the guidance and supervision of a healthcare provider. PYZCHIVA should only be administered to patients who will be closely monitored and have regular follow-up visits with a healthcare provider. The appropriate dose should be determined by a healthcare provider using the patient's current weight at the time of dosing. In pediatric patients, it is recommended that PYZCHIVA be administered by a healthcare provider. If a healthcare provider determines that it is appropriate, a patient may self-inject or a caregiver may inject PYZCHIVA after proper training in subcutaneous injection technique. Instruct patients to follow the directions provided in the Medication Guide [see Medication Guide].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: y It is recommended that each injection be administered at a different anatomic location (such as upper arms, gluteal regions, thighs, or any quadrant of abdomen) than the previous injection, and not into areas where the skin is tender, bruised, erythematous, or indurated. When using the singledose vial, a 1 mL syringe with a 27 gauge, ½ inch needle is recommended.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: y Prior to administration, visually inspect PYZCHIVA for particulate matter and discoloration. PYZCHIVA is a clear, colorless to light yellow, sterile and preservative-free solution. Do not use PYZCHIVA if it is discolored or cloudy, or if other particulate matter is present. PYZCHIVA does not contain preservatives; therefore, discard any unused product remaining in the vial and/or syringe.

blocks.text: 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: PYZCHIVA is contraindicated in patients with clinically significant hypersensitivity to ustekinumab products or to any of the excipients in PYZCHIVA [see Warnings and Precautions (5.5)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.1 Infections
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Ustekinumab products may increase the risk of infections and reactivation of latent infections. Serious bacterial, mycobacterial, fungal, and viral infections were observed in patients receiving ustekinumab products [see Adverse Reactions (6.1, 6.3)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Serious infections requiring hospitalization, or otherwise clinically significant infections, reported in clinical trials included the following:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: y Plaque Psoriasis: diverticulitis, cellulitis, pneumonia, appendicitis, cholecystitis, sepsis, osteomyelitis, viral infections, gastroenteritis and urinary tract infections.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: y Psoriatic arthritis: cholecystitis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: y Crohn's disease: anal abscess, gastroenteritis, ophthalmic herpes zoster, pneumonia, and listeria meningitis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: y Ulcerative colitis: gastroenteritis, ophthalmic herpes zoster, pneumonia, and listeriosis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5500909 820 3
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Avoid initiating treatment with PYZCHIVA in patients with any clinically important active infection until the infection resolves or is adequately treated. Consider the risks and benefits of treatment prior to initiating use of PYZCHIVA in patients with a chronic infection or a history of recurrent infection.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Instruct patients to seek medical advice if signs or symptoms suggestive of an infection occur while on treatment with PYZCHIVA and discontinue PYZCHIVA for serious or clinically significant infections until the infection resolves or is adequately treated.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.2 Theoretical Risk for Vulnerability to Particular Infections
section_path: 5.2 Theoretical Risk for Vulnerability to Particular Infections
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Individuals genetically deficient in IL-12/IL-23 are particularly vulnerable to disseminated infections from mycobacteria (including nontuberculous, environmental mycobacteria), salmonella (including nontyphi strains), and Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccinations. Serious infections and fatal outcomes have been reported in such patients.
section_path: 5.2 Theoretical Risk for Vulnerability to Particular Infections
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: It is not known whether patients with pharmacologic blockade of IL-12/IL-23 from treatment with ustekinumab products may be susceptible to these types of infections. Consider appropriate diagnostic testing (e.g., tissue culture, stool culture, as dictated by clinical circumstances).
section_path: 5.2 Theoretical Risk for Vulnerability to Particular Infections
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.3 Pre-treatment Evaluation for Tuberculosis
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Evaluate patients for tuberculosis infection prior to initiating treatment with PYZCHIVA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Avoid administering PYZCHIVA to patients with active tuberculosis infection. Initiate treatment of latent tuberculosis prior to administering PYZCHIVA. Consider anti-tuberculosis therapy prior to initiation of PYZCHIVA in patients with a past history of latent or active tuberculosis in whom an adequate course of treatment cannot be confirmed. Closely monitor patients receiving PYZCHIVA for signs and symptoms of active tuberculosis during and after treatment.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.4 Malignancies
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Ustekinumab products are immunosuppressants and may increase the risk of malignancy. Malignancies were reported among subjects who received ustekinumab in clinical trials [see Adverse Reactions (6.1)]. In rodent models, inhibition of IL-12/IL-23p40 increased the risk of malignancy [see Nonclinical Toxicology (13)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety of ustekinumab products has not been evaluated in patients who have a history of malignancy or who have a known malignancy.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: There have been post-marketing reports of the rapid appearance of multiple cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas in patients receiving ustekinumab products who had pre-existing risk factors for developing non-melanoma skin cancer. Monitor all patients receiving PYZCHIVA for the appearance of nonmelanoma skin cancer. Closely follow patients greater than 60 years of age, those with a medical history of prolonged immunosuppressant therapy and those with a history of PUVA treatment [see Adverse Reactions (6.1)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5500909 820 3
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.5 Hypersensitivity Reactions
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis and angioedema, have been reported with ustekinumab products [see Adverse Reactions (6.1, 6.3)]. If an anaphylactic or other clinically significant hypersensitivity reaction occurs, institute appropriate therapy and discontinue PYZCHIVA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.6 Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Two cases of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), also known as Reversible Posterior Leukoencephalopathy Syndrome (RPLS), were reported in clinical trials. Cases have also been reported in postmarketing experience in patients with psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis and Crohn's disease. Clinical presentation included headaches, seizures, confusion, visual disturbances, and imaging changes consistent with PRES a few days to several months after ustekinumab product initiation. A few cases reported latency of a year or longer. Patients recovered with supportive care following withdrawal of ustekinumab products.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Monitor all patients treated with PYZCHIVA for signs and symptoms of PRES. If PRES is suspected, promptly administer appropriate treatment and discontinue PYZCHIVA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.7 Immunizations
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Prior to initiating therapy with PYZCHIVA, patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations as recommended by current immunization guidelines. Patients being treated with PYZCHIVA should avoid receiving live vaccines. Avoid administering BCG vaccines during treatment with PYZCHIVA or for one year prior to initiating treatment or one year following discontinuation of treatment. Caution is advised when administering live vaccines to household contacts of patients receiving PYZCHIVA because of the potential risk for shedding from the household contact and transmission to patient.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Non-live vaccinations received during a course of PYZCHIVA may not elicit an immune response sufficient to prevent disease.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.8 Noninfectious Pneumonia
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Cases of interstitial pneumonia, eosinophilic pneumonia and cryptogenic organizing pneumonia have been reported during post-approval use of ustekinumab products. Clinical presentations included cough, dyspnea, and interstitial infiltrates following one to three doses. Serious outcomes have included respiratory failure and prolonged hospitalization. Patients improved with discontinuation of therapy and in certain cases administration of corticosteroids. If diagnosis is confirmed, discontinue PYZCHIVA and institute appropriate treatment [see Adverse Reactions (6.3)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The following adverse reactions have been reported during post-approval use of ustekinumab products. blocks.text: Respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal disorders: Interstitial pneumonia, eosinophilic pneumonia and cryptogenic organizing pneumonia.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In plaque psoriasis trials the safety of ustekinumab products in combination with immunosuppressive agents or phototherapy has not been evaluated. In psoriatic arthritis trials, concomitant MTX use did not appear to influence the safety or efficacy of ustekinumab. In Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis induction trials, immunomodulators (6-MP, AZA, MTX) were used concomitantly in approximately ��� of subjects and corticosteroids were used concomitantly in approximately ��� and ��� of Crohns disease and ulcerative colitis subjects, respectively. Upon initiation or discontinuation of PYZCHIVA in patients who are receiving concomitant CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, consider monitoring for therapeutic effect or drug concentration and adjust the individual dosage of the CYP substrate as needed. blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 7.3 Allergen Immunotherapy
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Ustekinumab products have not been evaluated in patients who have undergone allergy immunotherapy. Ustekinumab products may decrease the protective effect of allergen immunotherapy (decrease tolerance) which may increase the risk of an allergic reaction to a dose of allergen immunotherapy. Therefore, caution should be exercised in patients receiving or who have received allergen immunotherapy, particularly for anaphylaxis.

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Risk Summary
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Limited data from observational studies, published case reports, and postmarketing surveillance on the use of ustekinumab products during pregnancy are insufficient to inform a drug associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, and other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. Transport of human IgG antibody across the placenta increases as pregnancy progresses and peaks during the third trimester; therefore, ustekinumab products may be transferred to the developing fetus (see Clinical Considerations). In animal reproductive and developmental toxicity studies, no adverse developmental effects were observed in offspring after administration of ustekinumab to pregnant monkeys at exposures greater than 100 times the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD).

blocks.text: The background risk of major birth defects and miscarriage for the indicated population(s) are unknown. All pregnancies have a background risk of birth defect, loss, or other adverse outcomes. In the U.S.

blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Fetal/Neonatal Adverse Reactions
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Because ustekinumab products may theoretically interfere with immune response to infections, consider risks and benefits prior to administering live vaccines to infants exposed to PYZCHIVA in utero. There are insufficient data regarding exposed infant serum levels of ustekinumab products at birth and the duration of persistence of ustekinumab products in infant serum after birth. Although a specific timeframe to delay administration of live attenuated vaccines in infants exposed in utero is unknown, consider the risks and benefits of delaying a minimum of 6 months after birth because of the clearance of the product.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Data
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Animal Data
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Ustekinumab was tested in two embryo-fetal development toxicity studies in cynomolgus monkeys. No teratogenic or other adverse developmental effects were observed in fetuses from pregnant monkeys that were administered ustekinumab subcutaneously twice weekly or intravenously weekly during the period of organogenesis. Serum concentrations of ustekinumab in pregnant monkeys were greater than 100 times the serum concentration in patients treated subcutaneously with 90 mg of ustekinumab weekly for 4 weeks.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In a combined embryo-fetal development and pre- and post-natal development toxicity study, pregnant cynomolgus monkeys were administered subcutaneous doses of ustekinumab twice weekly at exposures greater than 100 times the MRHD from the beginning of organogenesis to Day 33 after delivery. Neonatal deaths occurred in the offspring of one monkey administered ustekinumab at 22.5 mg/kg and one monkey dosed at 45 mg/kg. No ustekinumab-related effects on functional, morphological, or immunological development were observed in the neonates from birth through six months of age.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 8.2 Lactation
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Risk Summary
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Limited data from published literature suggests that ustekinumab is present in human breast milk. There are no available data on the effects of ustekinumab products on milk production. The effects of local gastrointestinal exposure and limited systemic exposure in the breastfed infant to ustekinumab products are unknown. No adverse effects on the breastfed infant causally related to ustekinumab products have been identified in the published literature or postmarketing experience.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be considered along with the mother's clinical need for PYZCHIVA and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child from PYZCHIVA or from the underlying maternal condition.

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 8.4 Pediatric Use
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Plaque Psoriasis
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety and effectiveness of PYZCHIVA have been established for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in pediatric patients 6 to 17 years of age who are candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Use of PYZCHIVA in pediatric patients 12 to less than 17 years of age is supported by evidence from a multicenter, randomized, 60 week trial (Ps STUDY 3) of ustekinumab that included a 12 week, doubleblind, placebo-controlled, parallel group portion, in 110 pediatric subjects 12 years of age and older [see Adverse Reactions (6.1), Clinical Studies (14.2)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Use of PYZCHIVA in pediatric patients 6 to 11 years of age is supported by evidence from an openlabel, single-arm, efficacy, safety and pharmacokinetics trial (Ps STUDY 4) of ustekinumab in 44 subjects [see Adverse Reactions (6.1), Clinical Pharmacology (12.3)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety and effectiveness of PYZCHIVA have not been established in pediatric patients less than 6 years of age with plaque psoriasis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Psoriatic Arthritis
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety and effectiveness of PYZCHIVA have been established for treatment of psoriatic arthritis in pediatric patients 6 to 17 years old.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Use of PYZCHIVA in these age groups is supported by evidence from adequate and well controlled trials of ustekinumab in adults with psoriasis and PsA, pharmacokinetic data from adult subjects with psoriasis, adult subjects with PsA and pediatric subjects with psoriasis, and safety data of ustekinumab from two clinical trials in 44 pediatric subjects 6 to 11 years old with psoriasis and 110 pediatric subjects 12 to 17 years old with psoriasis. The observed pre-dose (trough) concentrations are generally comparable between adult subjects with psoriasis, adult subjects with PsA and pediatric subjects with psoriasis, and the PK exposure is expected to be comparable between adult and pediatric subjects with PsA [see Adverse Reactions (6.1), Clinical Pharmacology (12.3), and Clinical Studies (14.1, 14.2, 14.3)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety and effectiveness of PYZCHIVA have not been established in pediatric patients less than 6 years old with psoriatic arthritis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Crohn's Disease and Ulcerative Colitis
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety and effectiveness of PYZCHIVA have not been established in pediatric patients with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 8.5 Geriatric Use

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Of the 6709 subjects exposed to ustekinumab, a total of 340 were 65 years of age or older (183 subjects with plaque psoriasis, 65 subjects with psoriatic arthritis, 58 subjects with Crohn's disease and 34 subjects with ulcerative colitis), and 40 subjects were 75 years of age or older. Clinical trials of ustekinumab did not include sufficient numbers of subjects 65 years of age and older to determine whether they respond differently from younger adult subjects.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Ustekinumab products are KXPDQ ,J*1ԕ PRQRFORQDO DQWLERGies that bind with specificity to the p40 protein subunit used by both the IL-12 and IL-23 cytokines. IL-12 and IL-23 are naturally occurring cytokines that are involved in inflammatory and immune responses, such as natural killer cell activation and CD4+ T-cell differentiation and activation. In in vitro models, ustekinumab products were shown to disrupt IL-12 and IL-23 mediated signaling and cytokine cascades by disrupting the interaction of these cytokines with a shared cell- surface receptor chain, IL-125ȕ1.7KH F\WRNLQHV ,/-12 and IL-23 have been implicated as important contributors to the chronic inflammation that is a hallmark of Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. In animal models of colitis, genetic absence or antibody blockade of the p40 subunit of IL-12 and IL-23, the target of ustekinumab products, was shown to be protective.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Store PYZCHIVA vials, and prefilled syringes refrigerated between 2°C to 8°C (36°F to 46°F). Store PYZCHIVA vials upright. Keep the product in the original carton to protect from light until the time of use. Do not freeze. Do not shake.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If needed, individual prefilled syringes may be stored at room temperature up to 30°C (86°F) for a maximum single period of up to 35 days in the original carton to protect from light. If not used within 35 days of room temperature storage, discard the prefilled syringe. The prefilled syringe may be returned to the refrigerator one time only for a maximum of 60 days. If not used within 60 days, discard the prefilled syringe. Record the date when the prefilled syringe is removed from and returned to the refrigerator on the carton in the space provided.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Read this Instructions for Use before you start using PYZCHIVA. Your doctor or nurse should show you how to prepare, measure your dose, and give your injection of PYZCHIVA the right way.
section_path: Instructions for injecting PYZCHIVA from a vial.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If you cannot give yourself the injection:

section_path: Instructions for injecting PYZCHIVA from a vial.

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Important information:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Before you start, check the carton to make sure that it is the right dose. You will have either 45 mg or 90 mg as prescribed by your doctor.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: ƕ If your dose is 45 mg or less you will receive one 45 mg vial.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: ƕ If your dose is 90 mg, you will receive two 45 mg vials and you will need to give yourself two injections, one right after the other.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Children 12 years of age and older weighing less than 132 pounds require a dose lower than 45 mg.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Check the expiration date on the vial and carton. If the expiration date has passed, do not use it. If the expiration date has passed, call your doctor or pharmacist, or call Sandoz Inc. at 1-800525-8747 for help.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Check the vial for any particles or discoloration. Your vial should look clear and colorless to light yellow.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not use if it is frozen, discolored, cloudy or has particles. Get a new vial.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not shake the vial at any time. Shaking your vial may damage your PYZCHIVA medicine. If your vial has been shaken, do not use it. Get a new vial.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not use a PYZCHIVA vial more than one time, even if there is medicine left in the vial. After the rubber stopper is punctured, PYZCHIVA can become contaminated by harmful bacteria which could cause an infection if re-used. Therefore, throw away any unused PYZCHIVA after you give your injection.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Safely throw away (dispose of) PYZCHIVA vials after use.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not re-use syringes or needles. See "Step 6: Dispose of needles and syringes."
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: To avoid needle-stick injuries, do not recap needles.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Storage information
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Store PYZCHIVA in a refrigerator between 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Store PYZCHIVA vials standing up straight.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Store PYZCHIVA in the original carton to protect from light until the time of use.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not freeze PYZCHIVA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 1: Prepare the injection.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Choose a well-lit, clean, flat work surface.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Wash your hands well with soap and warm water.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 2: Prepare your injection site
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Choose an injection site around your stomach area (abdomen), buttocks, and upper legs (thighs).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: If a caregiver is giving you the injection, the outer area of the upper arms may also be used. (See Figure B)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Use a different injection site for each injection. Do not give an injection in an area of the skin that is tender, bruised, red or hard.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Clean the skin with an antiseptic wipe where you plan to give your injection.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not touch this area again before giving the injection. Let your skin dry before injecting.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not fan or blow on the clean area.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header

blocks.speaker: label

blocks.text: *Areas in gray are recommended injection sites.

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 3: Prepare the vial.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Remove the cap from the top of the vial. Throw away the cap but do not remove the rubber stopper. (See Figure C)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Figure C
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Clean the rubber stopper with an antiseptic swab. (See Figure D)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Figure D
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not touch the rubber stopper after you clean it.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Put the vial on a flat surface.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 4: Prepare the syringe
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Pick up the syringe with the needle attached.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Remove the cap that covers the needle. (See Figure E)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Throw the needle cap away. Do not touch the needle or allow the needle to touch anything.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Figure E
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5500909 820 3
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Carefully pull back on the plunger to the line that matches the dose prescribed by your doctor.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Hold the vial between your thumb and index (pointer) finger.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Use your other hand to push the syringe needle through the center of the rubber stopper. (See Figure F)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Figure F
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Push down on the plunger until all of the air has gone from the syringe into the vial.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Turn the vial and the syringe upside down. (See Figure G)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Hold the PYZCHIVA vial with one hand.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: It is important that the needle is always in the liquid in order to prevent air bubbles forming in the syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Pull back on the syringe plunger with your other hand.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Fill the syringe until the black tip of the plunger lines up with the mark that matches your prescribed dose.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Figure G
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5500909 820 3
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not remove the needle from the vial. Hold the syringe with the needle pointing up to see if it has any air bubbles inside.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: If there are air bubbles, gently tap the side of the syringe until the air bubbles rise to the top. (See Figure H)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Slowly press the plunger up until all of the air bubbles are out of the syringe (but none of the liquid is out).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Remove the syringe from the vial. Do not lay the syringe down or allow the needle to touch anything.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Figure H
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 5: Inject PYZCHIVA
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Hold the barrel of the syringe in one hand, between the thumb and index fingers.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not pull back on the plunger at any time.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5500909 820 3
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Use the other hand to gently pinch the cleaned area of skin. Hold firmly.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Use a quick, dart-like motion to insert the needle into the pinched skin at about a 45-degree angle. (See Figure I)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Figure I
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Push the plunger with your thumb as far as it will go to inject all of the liquid. Push it slowly and evenly, keeping the skin gently pinched.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: When the syringe is empty, pull the needle out of your skin and let go of the skin. (See Figure J)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Figure J
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: When the needle is pulled out of your skin, there may be a little bleeding at the injection site. This is normal. You can press a cotton ball or gauze pad to the injection site if needed. Do not
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5500909 820 3
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: rub the injection site. You may cover the injection site with a small adhesive bandage, if necessary.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If your dose is 90 mg, you will receive two 45 mg vials and you will need to give yourself a second injection right after the first. Repeat Steps 1 to 5 using a new syringe. Choose a different site for the second injection.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 6: Dispose of the needles and syringes.

blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not re-use a syringe or needle.
section_path: Step 6: Dispose of the needles and syringes.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: To avoid needle-stick injuries, do not recap a needle.
section_path: Step 6: Dispose of the needles and syringes.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Put your needles and syringes in an FDA-cleared sharps disposal container right away after use. Do not throw away (dispose of) loose needles and syringes in your household trash.

blocks.text: If you do not have an FDA-cleared sharps disposal container, you may use a household container that is:

blocks.text: ƕ made of heavy-duty plastic
section_path: Step 6: Dispose of the needles and syringes.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: ƕ can be closed with a tight-fitting, puncture-resistant lid, without sharps being able to come out
section_path: Step 6: Dispose of the needles and syringes.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: ƕ upright and stable during use
section_path: Step 6: Dispose of the needles and syringes.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: ƕ leak-resistant,
section_path: Step 6: Dispose of the needles and syringes.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: ƕ and properly labeled to warn of hazardous waste inside the container.
section_path: Step 6: Dispose of the needles and syringes.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: When your sharps disposal container is almost full, you will need to follow your community guidelines for the right way to dispose of your sharps disposal container. There may be local or state laws about how to throw away syringes and needles. For more information about safe sharps disposal, and for specific information about sharps disposal in the state that you live in, go to the FDA's website at: http://www.fda.gov/safesharpsdisposal.
section_path: Step 6: Dispose of the needles and syringes.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not dispose of your sharps disposal container in your household trash unless your community guidelines permit this. Do not recycle your sharps disposal container.
section_path: Step 6: Dispose of the needles and syringes.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Throw away the vial into the container where you put the syringes and needles.
section_path: Step 6: Dispose of the needles and syringes.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: If you have any questions, talk to your doctor or pharmacist.
section_path: Step 6: Dispose of the needles and syringes.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Keep PYZCHIVA and all medicines out of reach from children.
